explanation: In the United States, punctuality is a sign of respect and professionalism in business settings. Arriving late to a meeting is generally considered rude and can imply disorganization or lack of regard for others' time.
local_tip: Always aim to arrive 5 minutes early to a meeting, and if you are delayed, notify the organizer immediately with an estimated arrival time.
regional_note: In some parts of the South or in more relaxed industries (e.g., tech startups), a 5–10 minute grace period may be tolerated, but it is still safer to be on time.

also_check.note: Punctuality is extremely important; arriving even a minute late can be seen as disrespectful.
In São Paulo and Rio, business meetings often start 10–15 minutes late, but it is safer to arrive on time.
While some business meetings may start late due to traffic or flexible scheduling, arriving on time is still appreciated.
